about.title: Pleasant Hill Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Pleasant Hill residents rely on a mix of local clinics, urgent care centers, and larger Contra Costa County medical facilities for everything from routine checkups to emergency care. Most of the time, that care goes as expected. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes off course, or medication is mismanaged, the aftermath can leave a family with new injuries, extended recovery, and difficult questions about what actually happened. California treats these claims differently than a typical injury case — there's a shorter window to act, a required notice period before filing suit, and rules about what a claim must show. If you're trying to sort out whether what you experienced was simply an unfortunate outcome or something that fell below the expected standard of care, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases and can walk through what you're facing.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Move Forward

items.title: The Clock Starts Sooner Than You Might Think
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, but never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. Waiting to sort things out on your own can quietly shrink the time you have left to act.

items.title: A Notice Period Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed, California law requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider involved. Getting this step right matters, and an attorney familiar with the process can help make sure it's handled properly.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A bad medical outcome by itself isn't enough to prove malpractice — California requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on whether the care fell below the accepted standard. This is one reason early legal guidance can make a real difference in how a case is built.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery in Pleasant Hill — does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law recognizes that medicine carries inherent risk, and a poor result on its own doesn't establish malpractice. What matters is whether the care provided fell below the accepted medical standard, which is typically evaluated by a qualified medical expert.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred, whichever comes first. There's also a required 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed, so it's worth getting guidance sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, though that cap has been set to rise annually. An attorney can explain how this applies to your specific situation and what other types of damages, such as medical costs, may be recoverable.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything for connecting me with an attorney in Pleasant Hill?
items.answer: No — LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in the network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. We simply help you get in touch with an independent attorney who can evaluate your situation.
